title: Block motif — six round
subtitle: A 13 cm solid square block worked in the round to six rounds
excerpt: Six rounds from the magic ring build a 13 cm solid block using the same no-side-chain construction as the four-round version. The extra two rounds make this the right scale for lap blanket grids and cushion covers where the four-round version would be slightly too small.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 1 (1885), solid block chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A six-round solid block crochet motif in sage green DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Dense treble sides with chain-2 corners, 13 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished block measures 13 × 13 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Block motif — six round
chartDefinition.caption: Six rounds. Chain-2 corners; no side chain spaces. Side treble count grows by 3 per side per round.

glossaryTerms.definition: The number of trebles along one side of a block motif, not counting the corner clusters. In a solid block, this count grows by 3 with each new round.

content.text: The six-round block extends the four-round construction by two more rounds, adding 3 trebles per side on each round. The
reaches 15 per side on round 6, giving a 13 cm motif that works at the same scale as a standard patchwork square.
Work in a single colour for a clean tile, or switch colour at round 5 for a contrast border round. Both finishes join with whip stitch or crochet slip stitch along any edge.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 16 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Work rounds 1–4 as per the four-round block motif. For round 5, sl st to corner sp, ch 3, work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr into corner. Tr into every side treble across (12 per side from round 4). 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr into next corner. Continue around. (15 tr per side after round 5, 18 after round 6.) Fasten off on round 6.
Work the eight-round block for a 17 cm motif suitable for floor cushion covers. Or try the bavarian crochet square for a ridge-textured alternative.
